purpose: NUMERIC provider/adapter status vocabulary. Runtime control logic uses the numeric `code`; the `label` is human/UI display metadata ONLY and must never be a control-flow string. Numeric codes leave gaps so a new status can be slotted BETWEEN existing ones without renumbering. Single source — proofs + the preference graph read this, never a parallel literal. See docs/architecture/numeric-preference-graph.md.
control_rule: Display strings are for humans. Stable IDs are for references. Numeric codes are for control logic. Never branch on a status display string.

codes.label: candidate
codes.note: cataloged, contract-bound, not yet wired live

codes.label: emulated
codes.note: running via a local contract-compatible emulator

codes.label: active_external
codes.note: wired against a real external provider

codes.label: deprecated
codes.note: on the way out; do not select for new work

_compat: Legacy status strings (active/candidate/experimental/deprecated/quarantined/replaced/foil/reference) in external_capability_catalog.json map onto these codes; the catalog keeps its label for backward-compat and DERIVES the code. foil/reference/quarantined are non-adoptable (treated < 30).
